text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat began on Tuesday his first public visit to Israel, where he will hold talks with Israeli President Ezer Weizman.
Arafat emerged from an Israeli air force helicopter that ferried him from the Gaza Strip to Weizman's private residence in the seaside town of Caesarea in central Israel.
Arafat's visit was another sign of an easing of tensions between Israel and the PLO since a wave of violence last month killed 59 Palestinians and 15 Jews.

The Palestinian leader's only previous visit to Israel -- at night and without advance announcement -- was a condolence call on the widow of assassinated Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin last November in Tel Aviv.

Weizman greeted Arafat, who was wearing his trademark khaki uniform and chequered keffiyeh, at the entrance to his whitewashed villa in Caesarea, a seafront community that boasts Israel's only golf course.

The Israeli president, an architect of the 1979 Israeli-Egyptian peace treaty, was expected to discuss with Arafat the current Israel-PLO negotiations on Israel's long-delayed troop redeployment in the West Bank city of Hebron, Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh told Israel Radio.
